Why go: Koh Tao and Koh Nang Yuan

Koh Nang Yuan is three small islands off the north-west tip of Koh Tao, joined by a sandbar with a beach on each side. A climb of 15–25 minutes on steps and rock, with ropes on the steep parts, leads to the viewpoint where the classic photo of the three islands and the white sand spit is taken. Below it lies the Japanese Gardens, a shallow, sheltered reef a short swim from the sand that suits beginner snorkellers. Koh Tao itself, about 60 km north of Koh Samui past Koh Phangan, is Thailand's best-known dive island, with rocky bays where coral starts a few metres from shore.

This is a full speedboat day: hotel pickup at 07:30–08:30, a crossing of about 1.5–2 hours each way (with a stop at Koh Phangan on the way), Koh Nang Yuan for the sandbar, viewpoint and Japanese Gardens, a Thai lunch on Koh Tao, then two snorkelling bays chosen on the day, such as Mango Bay, Hin Wong or Aow Leuk. You are back on Samui in the late afternoon and at your hotel in the evening, about 9 hours door to door. Lunch, water, soft drinks, fruit and snorkel gear are included; the Nang Yuan island fee is paid in cash.

Honest comparison: this is the longest crossing of any of our day trips, and in a north-east wind it can be bumpy. In return you get the clearest water and the most varied snorkelling within day-trip range of Samui. It also runs all year, including 1 November–15 December, when Ang Thong Marine Park is closed. Those weeks are also the windiest of the year, so departures depend on the sea.

Who this tour is for

  • Snorkellers who want the best reefs within day-trip range of Samui.
  • Travellers who want the Nang Yuan viewpoint photo without moving islands.
  • Visitors from 1 November to 15 December looking for a full-day boat trip while Ang Thong is closed.
  • Families with children who handle long boat rides well. Children aged 3–11 pay the child price and infants up to 2 travel free.

Who should choose another tour

  • Prone to seasickness: the crossing is long and open; the Pig Island longtail stays in sheltered water.
  • Pregnant or with back problems: we don't advise a long speedboat crossing.
  • Want limestone cliffs, kayaking and a lagoon: the Ang Thong speedboat tour (from 16 December).
  • Want a short, easy day: the Pig Island speedboat tour.
  • Want to scuba dive: see diving from Koh Samui.
  • Want to stay on Koh Tao: the tour boat returns to Samui; take a ferry instead (see Koh Samui to Koh Tao).

What to bring

  • Cash for the Koh Nang Yuan fee: 250 THB per adult, paid on arrival. Small notes help.
  • A reusable water bottle: plastic bottles and cans are not allowed on Nang Yuan, and drinking water is provided on the boat.
  • Shoes with grip for the viewpoint climb.
  • Reef-safe sunscreen, a hat and sunglasses with a strap.
  • Swimwear, a towel and a change of clothes.
  • Seasickness tablets, taken an hour before departure.
  • A dry bag for phone and cash.

Good to know

  • Sea by month: February to September has the calmest crossings and the best visibility. October to January brings the north-east monsoon, with choppier water on the open Gulf and more weather cancellations. Rain alone doesn't cancel; strong wind and waves do. If we cancel, we tell you the evening before and you choose a full refund or a new date. Check the forecast on windy.com or our sea conditions page.
  • Nang Yuan rules: no plastic bottles or cans (bags are checked at the pier), no fins on the island's reef, and no drones over the island or the water around it. Day visitors are admitted from 10:00 to 15:00. Loungers and umbrellas cost extra, and food and drink on the island are sold only by the resort.
  • The viewpoint: at busy times expect a 10–20 minute wait for the photo spot. It is optional.
  • Snorkelling: stay inside the buoyed areas at the Japanese Gardens and never stand on coral. Don't swim across the channel between Nang Yuan and Koh Tao: it has strong currents and boat traffic.
  • Seasickness: sit towards the back of the boat, keep your eyes on the horizon and eat a light breakfast.
  • Children and non-swimmers: life jackets are provided for all ages and children wear them at all times on the boat. Snorkelling and the climb are optional.
  • No one-way drop-offs: the boat returns to Koh Samui at the end of the day.

Pickup and meeting point

Hotel transfers are included from the main areas of Koh Samui: Chaweng, Lamai, Bophut, Maenam, Choeng Mon, Bang Rak and Plai Laem. Remote areas (Nathon, Lipa Noi, Taling Ngam, Bang Kao, Thong Krut and similar) cost 400 THB per person return, added on the booking card. Pickup is 07:30–08:30, followed by check-in at the pier with a life-jacket fitting and safety briefing. We send your exact time and the pier location by email and WhatsApp the day before. Staying on Koh Phangan? The same trip runs from there at the same price: see tours on kohphangan.com.
